events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.50)
events.body:
RydeTAXI metered trip; the rider disputes a longer route and the fare. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists (F3, 22:54–23:03, 3.77 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, +2.13 km) and that no traffic incident on the replaced stretch qualifies under RD-4(a) (F15) [RD-1]. Only RD-5 can exempt the segment, and that is mine to read.

The chat is complete and fully timestamped [F10]: at 22:51 the driver asked “Looks like traffic on Pan Island Expressway is building up, mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?” [F8], and at 22:51 the rider answered “Sure, go ahead.” [F9]. That is a rider message sent before the segment started at 22:54, so it is genuine consent, not a mere claim in the driver's post-trip statement [F11] (G11). The rider's wording is a specific named-road agreement — “go round via Guillemard Road” — not a general “whichever way is faster” authorisation, so under RD-5 it covers driving on Guillemard Road only.

What the record does not do is tie the 22:54–23:03 segment to Guillemard Road. F3 gives only distance, duration, and an off-route measure up to 1095 m; the fact table carries no road name for the driven path, and no stop, no message placing the car on Guillemard Road, and no road-name fact exists [F3][F8][F9]. Nor does anything place the segment elsewhere, so this is the “nothing ties them” case: RD-5 + G13 → undetermined.

Because the segment is neither exempt nor counted, the RD-2 arithmetic cannot be executed: if Guillemard Road was driven, the segment is exempt and the amount is $0.00; if it was not, the amount would be 2.13 km × $1.4102/km (the distance fare ÷ distance km on this trip, F4) = $3.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The finding therefore changes the amount, and G13/G12 require the case to go to a person. I do not treat the missing path record as favouring either party [F3][F10].

The surplus of the trip total (+2.6 km, +9.1 min; F1, F2) I leave out of the ruling: the trace attributes only one off-route segment, and RD-2 does not refund mileage not assigned to a segment [RD-2]. The driver's account shows 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days (F18), which would trigger RD-6 account review only if the segment is later found non-exempt — so no flag is set now; the reviewer should apply RD-6 if the segment counts. Wait time billed was $0.11 (0.4 min) [F5], which on RydeTAXI is meter waiting and is not contested [RD-3(c)].

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: pull the trip path data for 22:54–23:03 and check whether the 3.77 km off-route segment ran on Guillemard Road (the road the rider agreed to at 22:51); if it did not, treat the segment as non-exempt under RD-2 and consider a partial refund plus an account review for the driver (2 prior upheld route disputes). No automated refund is issued.
